ActionId.description:
The one-click tool an area can be freed with (story "Whole disk: free
space with the owning tool"); this report only names it.

oneOf.description:
`conda env remove -p` of one `/opt` environment; its identifier is
the environment's path.

`conda clean` of one `/opt` install's package folder; its
identifier is the install's prefix.

`brew uninstall --formula` of one formula, every keg of it; its
identifier is the formula's `full_name` (story "Whole disk: Homebrew
packages, their sizes, and brew uninstall"). No area names it.

`brew uninstall --formula` of the formulae a removal left needed by
nothing; no identifier.

Capability.description:
What a platform can do beyond listing, measuring and removing files
(ADR "Platform seam", §3). A closed list in declaration order: a new
value bumps the schema version of every report that carries the list.

oneOf.description:
The clone-aware private size where clones are expected (APFS).
Without it `private_bytes` is never present.

The in-use checks before a delete (safety ADR §5). Its absence is no
permission to delete without them.
Evicted cloud files are recognised and never downloaded while scanning.

A permission system (TCC) can withhold parts of the home folder.
Without it `full_disk_access` is `true`.

Local backup snapshots that delay freeing space are counted. Without
it a clean report's `local_snapshots` is 0 and has no meaning.
`ddc disk` and the `disk free` actions on its rows.
`ddc disk agents`.
`ddc disk brew-packages` and the `disk free` actions on its rows.
`ddc schedule`.
The background scan shows a notification.

action.description: The `disk free` action that needs the absent capability.

capability.description: The capability this platform does not declare (`capability-absent`).

holders.description:
`busy` only: the live holders of the lock whose records were found;
empty when none wrote one, or where `in-use-check` is not declared.

owner.description:
The SID of the account that owns `root`, when it was read
(`root-not-owned`).

owner_unreadable.description:
`root-not-owned` only: true when the owner of `root`, or this
process's token, could not be read, so it is unknown whether `root`
is the user's.

platform.description: The platform the CLI was built for.

root.description:
The scan root that is not the user's (`root-not-owned`); the folder
asked about (`not-a-repository`); the main checkout
(`home-is-the-checkout`).

simulated.description:
True only in a build made with `simulate-unported`: the refusal is a
test build's, not the platform's.

oneOf.description:
The platform is not supported yet: only `--version`, `--help` and
`rules` run.

The platform does not declare the capability the command, or a
`disk free` action, needs.

A scan root another account owns, in an elevated terminal (Windows),
or one whose owner cannot be read there: refused with exit 2 before
anything is scanned or changed.

Another scan or clean holds the data-dir lock: exit 75, nothing was
touched. Carries `holders`.

`ddc agent footprint`: the folder is not inside a git repository
(exit 2). Carries `root`.

`ddc agent footprint`: the main checkout is the home folder; walking
it is a home scan (exit 2). Carries `root`, the main checkout.

Holder.description: One holder of the lock, as its record holds it.

phase.description: A clean's phase; absent for every other command.

progress.description: A clean's items done of its total, once its first item ran.

start_us.description:
The process's start, in microseconds since the epoch: the number in
the record's name.

started.description: The same start, RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second.

HolderCommand.description: What took the lock: one value per caller of `try_lock`.

HolderPhase.description: A clean's phase: what a SIGINT does to it.

oneOf.description:
Re-checking the items: no handler yet, a SIGINT ends it at once and
nothing has been removed.
The executor runs: a SIGINT stops it after its current item.

LockMode.description: Scans share the lock; a cleanup takes it exclusively.

Origin.description: Where the holder was started. A guess, for the words only.

oneOf.description:
The binary runs from an app bundle's `Contents/Helpers/`, without a
terminal.
stdin or stderr is a terminal.
Anything else: a script, a launch agent, a pipe.

Platform.description: The operating system a build is for, as `std::env::consts::OS` names it.
